q8.answer: The MERGE matches on order_id and updates only when s.updated_at >= t.updated_at, so an older copy never overwrites a newer one. Equal versions overwrite with identical data, so overlap re-extracts and re-runs are harmless. Staging is also deduped, keeping the max updated_at per order_id, before the merge.

q9.answer: It is stored in the warehouse, in etl.watermark: one row for pipeline='orders', column high_water_mark, seeded to the epoch. The value written is GREATEST(current, new_hwm), where new_hwm = max(updated_at) of the batch with no 2h subtraction (the lookback is applied only when reading it). It is written inside the single commit transaction, together with the merge and the run_log committed update, and skipped if the batch was empty.

q10.answer: analytics.orders changes only in one atomic warehouse transaction (merge, watermark, run_log) and dashboards read only that table, never staging. With snapshot isolation for readers, which is listed under Assumptions to confirm, they see either the previous complete state or the new complete state.

q11.answer: Nothing needs cleaning up. Staging is truncated at the start of every attempt, and the target and watermark were unchanged because they only change in the final commit. The retry runs from the start and extracts the same window, updated_at > HWM minus 2h, since the watermark did not move. If the night turns out to be already committed, the retry exits 0 instead.

q12.answer: For each mismatched creation day it re-reads all replica rows with created_at on that day (UTC), via stg.orders_reconcile, which is truncated at the start of each day's reload. It applies them with the same MERGE, with the >= guard, in a per-day transaction. It never touches the nightly high-water mark.
